content: Penciclovir cream is prescribed for use on the lips and face of adults to treat cold sores caused by the herpes simplex virus. While it does not cure herpes infections, it can reduce pain and itching if applied at the earliest signs of symptoms. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Penciclovir is available as a cream and is typically applied externally every two hours while awake for a duration of four days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to clarify any part you do not understand. Use penciclovir exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Apply the medication as soon as possible after symptoms appear. Before applying the cream, clean and dry the affected area to prevent spreading the infection. Gently rub the cream into the skin, ensuring that all sores are completely covered. Continue using penciclovir even if you feel better, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Before using penciclovir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to penciclovir, acyclovir (Zovirax), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using penciclovir, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to apply a dose, use it as soon as you remember and apply the remaining doses for that day at evenly spaced intervals. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Penciclovir may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: headache or irritation at the site of application. Store this medication in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature and away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the appropriate disposal method. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Penciclovir should only be used on the lips and face, and you should avoid getting it in your eyes. Keep the infected area clean and dry. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the penciclovir treatment, contact your doctor.
